sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Waddar language' (en; also kn, es stubs). Accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; lists Sarikar 1998 (hdl:10603/96379) and Ghodke 2017 (hdl:10603/257238) as further reading, Zvelebil 1990 p. 57 and Bhat 1984 (ethnography) as sources.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Vadari' section, pp. 607-619.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3254.1 F; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 5.40; a Harvard library, call number Ud 0010
sources.note: Silent. Grierson calls Vadari 'simply vulgar Telugu' and gives only segmental substitutions (a for o in postpositions, ch > s, k/g interchange), a few morphological notes, and four specimens (Bijapur, Belgaum, Sholapur, Jamkhandi, Akola); no accent or stress statement anywhere in pp. 607-619 (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress in that span: nothing).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid wadd1237 (Waddar); ISO 639-3 page for wbq.
sources.note: Nothing; Glottolog lists Sarikar 1998 (grammar) and Grierson 1906 only. The Wintz 1909 Dyola dictionary attached to wadd1237 in our our source list dump is a mis-linked record (Dyola is a Senegalese language), not a Waddar source.
